set.st: George M. Vollmer of Stillwater, supposed to be rich, died in the fall of 1899 and little property could be found. His will left nearly everything to his sons George and Emil, and the daughters contested it; the special administrator and other parties got leave to search the house and found money of all kinds hidden in cracks and crevices everywhere, an estimated $7,000 to $10,000. He had always considered banks unsafe, and the search was to go on until every article in the house was examined. Pin is the house address from the 1900 census (his widow still lived there). Records check: Correction: the will left nearly all the property to the sons George and Emil Vollmer; the daughters contested it in Washington Co. probate court (Judge Wilson) in Nov. 1899. The special administrator and other parties got leave to search the house and found wads of $40 to $900 in every conceivable place; some contestants thought more remained. A Washington Co. probate file exists (contest). His December 1898 will left each of his five daughters $5 and the rest to his two sons, which explains the contest that followed.
set.t: Found in 1899, so this is a lesson more than a target: bank-shy townsmen hid money in the house itself, in walls and cracks, not in the yard. The 1900 census puts his widow at 305 S. Main St; if the house still stands, look only. Private property.
set.pl: 305 S. Main St, Stillwater (1900 census, the widow's household)
pinev: 1894 and 1898 Stillwater directories list George Vollmer on 'S Main' with no house number.
1900 US census, Stillwater Ward 2, sheet 1: Margaret Volmer, 79, b. 1820 Germany, widow, head, with niece Othilie, at 305 So. Main St, a few months after the 1899 search.

Placed from modern MnGeo address points: 301 S Main is at 45.0549,-92.8053 (E side) and 302-308 at 45.0547,-92.8057 (W side); r80 covers both sides of the 300 block. Whether the 1900 numbering matches today's is not checked.

pinev: Lexington Twp (T111N R24W) centre, from BLM PLSS section corners; the Duluth News Tribune 1906 original names the Martin Millet farm in Lexington Twp. Farm not yet placed on a plat.

1898 Le Sueur plat (Ancestry image 31617_072135-00499): a Reinhardt family tract ('S. Reinhardt 83'), N half sec 18 T111N R25W (Sharon Twp), ~44.424,-93.884, ~7 mi S of Henderson; whether it is the 1858 Reinhart clearing is unproven.

1860 census puts a Sebastian Reinhardt household in Sharon Twp, tying the 1898 'S. Reinhardt 83' tract (N sec 18 T111N R25W, 44.424,-93.884) to the 1858 family; that clearing is the likely murder site, the Millet farm the 1906 find site.
Reinhardt household present in Sharon Twp 1860, absent 1870 (no 1857 index hit); an heir holds the tract on the 1898 plate. Inconclusive for the 1858 hanging tale.
